source.author: stat
source.text: Taenariis hic celsus equis, quam dispare coetu Cyllarus ignaro generarat Castore prolem, quassat humum; vatem cultu Parnassia monstrant vellera: frondenti crinitur cassis oliva albaque puniceas interplicat infula cristas, arma simul pressasque iugo moderatur habenas.
source.text_original: Taenariis hic celsus equis, quam dispare coetu / Cyllarus ignaro generarat Castore prolem, / quassat humum; vatem cultu Parnassia monstrant / vellera: frondenti crinitur cassis oliva / albaque puniceas interplicat infula cristas, / arma simul pressasque iugo moderatur habenas.
source.text_english: Here, mounted high on Taenarian horses, he shakes the ground, by how unlike a troupe Cyllarus had begotten offspring for Castor, unaware of the deed; the fleeces, by their adornment, point out the prophet of Parnassus. His helmet is crowned with leafy olive, and a white fillet entwines the scarlet plumes; at the same time he controls his arms and the reins, taut under the yoke.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: hic vates Phoebique fides non vana parentis Mopsus, puniceo cui circumfusa cothurno palla imos ferit alba pedes vittataque fronte cassis et in summo laurus Peneia cono.
reuse.text_original: hic vates Phoebique fides non vana parentis / Mopsus, puniceo cui circumfusa cothurno / palla imos ferit alba pedes vittataque fronte / cassis et in summo laurus Peneia cono.
reuse.text_english: Here is that seer, and the trustworthy, no-false son of Phoebus, Mopsus, around whom a scarlet cloak hangs, striking his feet at the bottom; on his brow a helmet bound with ribbons, and on the top of the crest the Peneian laurel.
